scope: Read-only source audit of frozen Windows ABI19 reentry fixture; no cause established, no production edits or new workflow
head: e8c284445b394fa99dcf04f332cc43bcdf914dac

observations.finding: Fixture explicitly enables native_frame_calls, stress_steps, oracle and quarantine; shrink_to_fit forces task-vector growth during metamethod callback. Existing logs do not identify precompile versus either scheduled run phase.
spawn invalidates frame context before tasks.push. call_value creates a scratch task for the metamethod callback.
Nested compiled entry refreshes for its task, then restores native_task and invalidates context after return.
GetField slow path uses hcall j_get_field_ic; unknown helper effects include REENTERS, so generated code calls j_frame_refresh after successful helper return.
j_frame_refresh rebuilds current and stack pointers when invalid; direct return reloads them from FrameContext. No missing refresh was demonstrated by this audit.
TRACE_CALLS sets it.trace; j_frame_refresh enables native fast calls only when !it.trace. TRACE_CALLS is not a neutral diagnostic control for this failure.

Compiled root walker reads fp+8 and fp, follows increasing frame pointers, and has an iteration cap but no thread-stack extent check. Rust build configuration forces frame pointers; JIT sets preserve_frame_pointers.

hypotheses: A stale task/frame pointer remains possible, but intended invalidation and refresh calls are present and no stale address was observed.
An invalid native frame-chain link is another possible access-violation site. Source inspection alone does not establish it as the cause or establish Windows ABI incompatibility.
GC/root liveness and code generation remain unexcluded because the fixture combines native calls and forced collection.
nextUsefulProbe: Test-only fixed phase markers before and after native_vm/precompile and each scheduled/non-scheduled run, without setting TRACE_CALLS.
Fixed-capacity nonallocating event records at spawn and refresh containing native_task, task vector base, current address, stack base and valid bit; compare refreshed addresses to the live task.
Record last native root-walk fp, return address and next link before dereference; do not silently skip suspect roots.
A postmortem dump from a plain-launched Windows test process can capture the fault without launching under GDB, which masks this failure. This is a proposed probe, not new remote authorization.
